evidence.detail: The class extends the live overlay base rs/l/f/b, registers itself on the overlay layer rs/l/f/a.v, and renders one current TransientMessageEntry each frame.

If a message is already active, new three-String entries are queued; exact duplicate triples are rejected, queue size is capped at three by dropping index 0 before append, and queued entries are promoted to the current slot when it becomes empty.

The overlay clears the current entry when System.currentTimeMillis() minus the entry timestamp reaches exactly 5000 milliseconds, resetting the promoted queued entry timestamp when it becomes current.

proposals.note: TransientMessageOverlay is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for the live queued five-second message overlay. 'TransientMessage' avoids inventing a feature/domain noun; confidence is 0.999.

evidence.detail: The class owns exactly three packet-provided Strings plus one creation timestamp and renders the first line with Client.gn and the second/third lines with Client.gl.

Construction timestamps the entry with System.currentTimeMillis(); the owning overlay removes the current entry after exactly 5000 ms, so the record is explicitly short-lived rather than persistent UI state.
The entry calculates width from the three rendered Strings, starts at width 175 and height 5, expands width then height, and renders a temporary bordered/filled panel before the SHOWING state.

proposals.note: TransientMessageEntry is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for one three-line, timestamped, animated message record shown by the ScriptPacket 23 overlay. The binary supplies no narrower content domain; confidence is 0.999.

evidence.detail: The enum constants survive exactly as EXPANDING_WIDTH, EXPANDING_HEIGHT and SHOWING.
TransientMessageEntry initializes to EXPANDING_WIDTH, advances to EXPANDING_HEIGHT when target width is reached, and then advances to SHOWING after target height is reached.

proposals.note: TransientMessageAnimationState follows exact surviving animation-state constants and their exclusive use by TransientMessageEntry. Confidence is 0.999.
